story: On a sunny Sunday afternoon at 4:17 on Magnolia Loop, Gary, Donna, Hal, and Rosa are gathered in the street with the golf carts parked nearby. Rosa has proposed a memorial hospital theme for the holiday parade, complete with ambulance carts and bandaged flamingos, while Gary eagerly promises wiring sketches by tomorrow. Hal, gruffly pleased to be the inspector, insists on sticking to the rulebook, and Donna, energized as ever, vows to keep her flock at three and tally everyone's ideas for the bulletin board.

gary.thought_process: Donna, Hal, and Rosa are all here and the committee sheet is up. At tick 200 I promised Rosa I'd sketch lights and wiring for all four carts, but she hasn't said her theme yet. I filed the Architectural Review application back at tick 156, so my cart stays in the garage until they sign off. Rather than ask Rosa again, I should answer Hal's inspector line and move things forward: offer him my wiring drawings to check against the rules, which also helps Hal see I'm careful. That keeps me useful and legal.

parameters.content: Good to have an inspector, Hal. I'll have my wiring sketches done by tomorrow, and you can go over every line against the rules before a single bulb goes on a cart.

donna.thought_process: Hal just confirmed three flamingos is the limit, and I'm the committee chair, so I should keep the peace and keep momentum. Rosa already pinned the committee note, Gary is sketching cart designs, and Hal has his inspector job. I shouldn't repeat anything I've said. The next useful step is to rally everyone toward concrete decisions: a theme, and a quick meeting so we win the cart prize within the rules. I'll address Rosa since she just posted the note and the group is clustered here, and propose we settle on a theme at the Town Square tomorrow while Gary gets his drawings done. Also keep Hal happy by promising his flamingos stay at three.

parameters.content: Love the note, Rosa. Hal, my flock stays at three, I promise. Let's all bring theme ideas to the bulletin board by tomorrow, and I'll tally them up so Gary can start sketching the carts.

hal.thought_process: Everyone's on the Loop, and the committee notes are already pinned up. I've been named decoration inspector, and a supply sergeant knows a job needs a standard. Rosa's planning the parade theme and Gary's sketching wiring tonight, so now is the time to lay out the rules plainly: three ornaments from the street, anything on the carts goes through Architectural Review first, and holiday lighting is legal only from Thanksgiving. That keeps them from handing me a violation later. I'm a little pleased to be asked, though I won't say so.

parameters.content: Saw the sign-up, Rosa. I'll inspect, but I go by the book: three ornaments from the street, no cart changes without review, and holiday lights aren't legal until Thanksgiving. Keep the parade inside that and I'll have nothing to write.

rosa.thought_process: Gary asked me to pick a theme so he can sketch the cart lights tonight, and I haven't answered yet. Hal is volunteering as inspector, Donna's sign-up sheet is up, and everyone's here in line-of-sight. Time to decide so Gary can actually work tonight. A Miami ER nurse's parade entry should be fun: a 'Magnolia Loop Memorial Hospital' theme, carts as ambulances and a crash cart, flamingos as patients in bandages. I'll keep it all legal and on paper per Hal and the board. This also keeps the Loop together on one project.

parameters.content: Theme's 'Magnolia Loop Memorial Hospital,' Gary. Four carts as ambulances with red and blue lights, and Donna's flamingos get bandages. Sketch it on paper, and Hal can sign off on the rules.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
